jobs.title: HR Business Partner
jobs.description:
We have a fantastic opportunity for an experienced and commercially minded HR Business Partner to join our Senior Leadership Team. This role will be remote with national travel and ideally based in the Midlands/North.

  

The HR Business Partner will act as a trusted adviser and coach to leaders, helping to develop management capability, strengthen leadership effectiveness and embed a culture of accountability, performance and continuous improvement. The role combines strategic business partnering with practical operational support, ensuring that people initiatives align with organisational objectives and contribute to improved business performance.

  

As a key member of the Regional Leadership Team, you will influence decision\-making, shape workforce strategies and lead the implementation of people initiatives that support growth, colleague engagement, service excellence and organisational effectiveness.

 **Benefits for the role include**

  

* Competitive Salary
* Annual car allowance
* Annual 10% Performance related bonus
* Private Healthcare
* 33 days annual leave (inclusive of bank holidays) with the option to purchase additional leave through salary sacrifice
* Life Assurance
* 24/7 online/telephone GP Consultation and access to prescriptions.
* 2nd opinion medical support following diagnosis or where a colleague is on a treatment pathway.
* Cash\-plan benefits, providing colleagues the option of protecting themselves in case of illness and recuperation, including dental, optical, chiropody.
* Access to mental health and physiotherapy consultations.
* Access to legal advice on domestic issues e.g. motoring offences, wills and probate, and personal injury.
* Long Service Recognition Scheme – recognising colleagues for their continued service after 5 years and at 5\-year intervals with an increase in annual leave.

  


**Role Responsibilities**

  

* Partner with Regional Directors and leadership teams to develop and deliver regional people plans that support operational, commercial and organisational objectives.
* Provide strategic HR advice on business planning, organisational development, workforce transformation and growth.
* Ensure people considerations are embedded in regional decision\-making and operational planning.
* Use workforce data, trends and insight to identify organisational risks, opportunities and targeted interventions.
* Lead and support organisational change, restructures, acquisitions, contract mobilisations and TUPE transfers.
* Coach, mentor and constructively challenge leaders to improve their confidence and effectiveness in managing people.
* Build capability in performance management, attendance, wellbeing, employee relations, talent development and colleague engagement.
* Identify leadership capability gaps and implement practical, measurable development solutions.
* Design and facilitate leadership workshops, management training and development interventions.
* Promote a culture in which managers take ownership and accountability for leading, developing and engaging their teams.
* Provide expert guidance on complex employee relations matters, ensuring compliance with employment legislation, organisational policy and good practice.
* Work collaboratively with specialist People colleagues to mitigate legal, employee relations, financial and reputational risk.
* Lead and support workforce planning, succession planning and talent management activity across the region.
* Drive colleague engagement activity and ensure feedback is translated into clear and meaningful action.
* Help embed a positive, inclusive and high\-performance culture aligned with EMED values and behaviours.
* Build credible and productive relationships with operational leaders, senior stakeholders, employee representatives and trade unions.
* Influence decisions at senior level through clear advice, professional expertise and constructive challenge.
* Represent the People Function at Regional Leadership Team meetings and operational forums.
* Support client presentations, bids, contract mobilisations and business development activity where appropriate.
* This role supports a geographically dispersed operational workforce and requires a significant and consistent regional presence. The successful candidate will: Travel regularly throughout the designated region to support operational locations and management teams.
* Spend time in operational environments to understand local challenges and identify effective people solutions.
* Attend regional and national meetings, leadership events, workshops and project activity. Undertake occasional overnight stays where business needs require.
* Success in the role will be assessed through agreed objectives and measures, including: Delivery and impact of regional people plans.

  


**Do you have what it takes?**

  


* CIPD Level 5 qualification or above, or equivalent professional experience.
* Significant experience operating as an HR Business Partner within a complex, multi\-site organisation.
* A proven record of strategic business partnering with senior operational leaders.
* Strong coaching and leadership development experience, with evidence of building management capability.
* Extensive knowledge of UK employment law and employee relations practice.
* Experience of leading and supporting organisational change and transformation.
* Demonstrable commercial awareness and the ability to connect people priorities with business outcomes.
* Experience of working in a unionised environment.
* Excellent communication, influencing and stakeholder management skills.
* The ability to interpret people data and turn insight into practical, targeted action.

  


**Desirable**

  

* Chartered CIPD membership.
* Experience within healthcare, emergency services, logistics, transport or another operationally intensive sector.
* Experience supporting large, geographically dispersed workforces.
* Experience of TUPE transfers, bids and contract mobilisat

jobs.title: HR People and Culture Trustee Advisor
jobs.description:
Leonard Cheshire is one of the UK’s leading disability charities, supporting disabled people to live, learn and work as independently as they choose. With around 100 services and more than 3,000 colleagues across the UK, our people and culture are fundamental to delivering safe, high\-quality, person\-centred support.  


We are seeking an experienced senior HR, People \& Culture or organisational development leader to join our Service Quality Committee as a co\-opted member.  


This is a strategic governance and advisory role, providing independent insight, constructive challenge and support to Trustees and senior executives as Leonard Cheshire continues its transformation and modernisation journey.  


What you’ll bring  


You will have significant senior\-level experience in areas such as:  


Organisational culture and development  
Leadership and management development  
People and culture strategy  
Workforce transformation and planning  
Learning and development  
Large\-scale organisational change  


You will be a strategic thinker with sound judgement and the confidence to provide constructive challenge at Board level. Experience in health, social care, regulated or charitable organisations would be advantageous.  


Your impact  


You will help the Service Quality Committee and Board to:  


Understand how culture, leadership and workforce capability influence service quality.  
Strengthen oversight of workforce and people\-related risks.  
Support organisational culture and transformation.  
Consider future workforce capability, leadership and succession.  
Ensure the voice, outcomes and lived experience of people we support remain central to decision\-making.  
You will also act as a strategic sounding board to the Executive Director of People on culture change, leadership capability, employee engagement, talent, succession, organisational effectiveness and workforce sustainability.  
Time commitment  


The role involves approximately four three\-hour Committee meetings per year, preparation and review of papers, with occasional attendance at Trustee development or strategy sessions.  


This is an exciting opportunity to contribute your expertise to a leading disability charity, while gaining valuable experience of charity governance and potentially progressing towards a future Trustee appointment.  


We particularly welcome applications from disabled people and people with lived experience of social care services. Reasonable adjustments will be supported throughout the process.  


A satisfactory disclosure check and references will be required.  


If you are a senior HR, People \& Culture or organisational development professional who wants to use your expertise to make a meaningful difference, we would love to hear from you.  


For more information, please contact Richard Pearson on 07734972684\.  


Job Types: Part\-time, Volunteer  


Work Location: Remote
